title: The 35.68-day GJ 832 wave from 2016-2018 increases 2019 squared error in upgraded HARPS data
abstract: We test whether a fixed 35.68-day wave predicts later GJ 832 velocities. A wave fitted to 54 upgraded-HARPS measurements from 2016-2018 raises weighted squared error in 56 measurements from 2019 by 36.6% with linear slow trends and 26.6% with quadratic trends. The fitted phase changes by 0.41 to 0.43 cycle. All tested periods from 35.55 to 35.82 days give negative prediction gains. Daily means, weight changes, and a fixed published giant-planet curve retain the error increase. Exact conditional sign tests depend on the noise blocks: 30-day tail fractions range from 0.0127 to 0.0586, while 100-day fractions range from 0.0625 to 0.125. We make no noise-model-independent rejection claim. A broader comparison of 62 older and 110 later HARPS rows gives a small positive gain under the main slow model. Independent ASH2 photometry shows brightness variation on the relevant time scale but does not confirm a velocity phase. Prior studies already favor stellar activity for this system. We report a limited prediction test, no new planet, and no planet exclusion. Raw snapshots, exact hashes, source code, simulations, figures and offline instructions are included. Job sci-1107-hp-astronomy-5eeedf8745c2; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: The within-upgrade test at 35.68 days. The first two panels show partial residuals after removal of jointly fitted slow curves and fitted wave coefficients. Error bars use the quoted error plus a fixed 2 m/s term in quadrature. The lower left panel shows every stated test period. The lower right panel shows exact conditional tail fractions under shared-wave residual signs, HC2 scaling, and different calendar blocks. The dashed 0.05 line is a reference, not a claim of robust significance.

The broad 62-row HARPS to 110-row HARPS+ comparison gives a small positive main-model gain. The phase panels use joint-fit partial residuals. The initial null panel uses separate-wave residuals; the preferred conservative shared-residual results are in the tables. Stable-wave replacements test sensitivity in the observed residuals and are not survey completeness.

Independent ASH2 B and V nightly means show broad brightness variation. There are 17 shared nights per filter over 51.8 days. The fixed 35.68- and 37.5-day scales are shown. The curves have no false-alarm calibration and do not confirm the velocity phase.
